raw_response:
I'm 68 this year, been farming this land since I was 18. Never spent a day in school, but I've got 50 years of dirt under my nails. It's just me and my old man now — two mouths, two pairs of hands, 15 and a half mu. Our boy is in Shijiazhuang working construction. He sends a bit when he can, but I don't count on it.

My main crop is Chinese cabbage, 6 mu on the good flat land by the well. That's what puts food on the table. I also keep 4 mu of cotton — old habit, though my back hates the picking. Three mu of maize for the chickens and some pocket money. Two mu of chili because the price was decent last year at the county market. And half a mu of spring cabbage, early stuff for eating and selling in June.

I do what I know works. Last year Old Wang tried some new fertilizer his son bought online and half his cabbage rotted. I'll stick to my way. For the Chinese cabbage, after the spring crops come off in June, my old man plows with the small tractor. We spread two cartloads of manure per mu — saved from our chickens and the neighbor's pigs. Then I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the kind with the three numbers on it. I buy the hybrid seeds from Old Zhang's shop, same kind as last year. Plant late July when the worst heat passes. Water four times — planting, twice in August when it's wrapping, and once before harvest. The well water isn't free anymore, they put a meter on it, so I watch it, but cabbage can't go dry. When the heads start forming, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. For worms, I spray when I see holes. I hire three village women for transplanting and harvest — 120 yuan a day each. My knees can't do that bending anymore.

Cotton goes in mid-April. One bag of compound per mu as base. Bt seeds, the ones with poison in them. Still have to spray twice for bollworm — the poison doesn't get them all. Water three times. Picking is the killer. I hire four people for the main picking, costs me near 1,500 yuan, but I can't do it alone.

Maize is easy. Mid-April, half a bag of compound per mu. Plant, water if it doesn't rain, spray for weeds once. My nephew combines it end of August, I just pay for diesel.

Chili seedlings go in late May. Manure and compound for base. Water four times. Picking from July to October, little by little. I do most of it, but hire two girls for the heavy days in September.

Spring cabbage on the half-mu — manure, a little compound, plant early April, harvest in June. No fuss.

Money is tight. Fertilizer went up again, urea is robbery now. I need about 6,000 yuan for everything. I've got 4,000 saved from last year's cabbage. I'll need to find another 2,000 — maybe my son can send it, or I'll sell one of the old sows. I hate borrowing. If cabbage prices hold, we'll be fine. If they crash... well, we've eaten plain noodles before and we'll do it again. At my age, I don't gamble. I do what worked before.
